title: StableBar scene
description: One screen that StableBar --render-scenes draws offscreen. A scene runs nothing: its outputs, history and workspaces replace every command, provider and window manager.

configuration.description: A StableBar configuration, or the path of one relative to this file.

outputs.description: Script outputs by widget id or provider name: an object as a script prints it, or plain text.

history.description: Graph samples by widget id or provider name.

desktopShortcuts.description: Switch to Desktop shortcuts enabled on the stand-in Mac, for setup and Settings. All off by default; workspaces supplies the desktops that exist.

activeApp.description: The active app's bundle identifier. Finder by default.

menu.description: The menu a popup scene shows in place of the widget's popup, as an app menu widget opens one: its items, with the values Accessibility gives a menu item.

title.description: The item's title. An empty title is a separator.

virtualKey.description: AXMenuItemCmdVirtualKey: the virtual key code of a key without a character.

glyph.description: AXMenuItemCmdGlyph: the menu glyph of a key without a character.

modifiers.description: AXMenuItemCmdModifiers: 0 is ⌘ alone, then 1 adds ⇧, 2 ⌥, 4 ⌃, 8 removes ⌘ and 16 adds fn. 0 by default.

enabled.description: Whether the item can be chosen. True by default.

checked.description: Whether the item has a checkmark.

submenu.description: Whether the item opens a submenu.

draw.description: What to draw. `update` draws the update popup for a sample offer, with the request for a star on GitHub. `setup` draws a step of setup's tour, 1512 by 982 points by default, with the bar above it as the configuration has it: setup's choices show in the tour, not on the bar, since previewing them would start the commands of the widgets they add. `accessibilityGuide` draws the panel that asks people to drag StableBar into the Accessibility list in System Settings.

widget.description: The widget whose popup or Settings page to draw.

section.description: The Settings section to draw when no widget is named.

tab.description: The tab of the widget's Settings page: content, style or behavior. With section bar and no widget, the tab of the bar's settings: size, look or placement.

uninstall.description: What the Uninstall sheet shows for a sample Mac: its confirmation, or the steps that failed before StableBar quits. The confirmation by default.

setup.description: For `setup`: the step to draw, the choices made before it, and what setup reads from the Mac, pinned so the drawing doesn't depend on the Mac that draws it. Every key is optional.

step.description: The step of the tour: where the bar goes, its look, the finishing touches, the permissions, or Try your bar. placement by default.

placement.description: The first step's choice, made before drawing: Replace the menu bar (top) or Keep the menu bar (belowMenuBar). Without it, neither is picked.

preset.description: The preset picked on the second step.

menuBarHides.description: Whether macOS hides its menu bar automatically. false by default.

accessibility.description: Whether macOS allows StableBar Accessibility. true by default.

automation.description: Whether macOS lets StableBar control System Events, which hiding or showing the menu bar needs. true by default.

calendars.description: Whether macOS allows StableBar full Calendar access. true by default.

battery.description: Whether the Mac has an internal battery, which presets add Battery for. true by default.

notch.description: Whether any connected display has a notch, which the Notch preset needs. true by default.

inApplications.description: Whether StableBar runs from an Applications folder, which Open at login needs. true by default.

appearances.description: The appearances to draw, each to its own image. Both by default.

accessibilityDisplay.description: For `bar` and `popup`: the settings of System Settings → Accessibility → Display to draw with. The others are off, whatever the Mac that draws has. macOS turns on Reduce transparency with Increase contrast, so list both to draw what a Mac with Increase contrast shows.
